messages:
alex: Quick smoke test summary: ran readloop sampling comparing continuous-stream vs batched-nonstream for 1k synthetic sessions over 10m. Observed ~12	6% latency regression for streaming on A100 q8 when KV hit-rate < 60%.

maria: which kernel did the selector pick? any fallback churn?

alex: KernelSelector logs: chose matmul_fused_v2 for seq>=128, matmul_naive for seq<64. But with streaming we see rapid oscillation between kernels as effective batch sizes hit/leave thresholds. Command used:
```
./bench --mode readloop --clients 1000 --duration 600 --streaming=true --kv-hit-rate 0.5
```

cheng: can you paste p50/p95 numbers?

alex: Results (aggregate):
kv_hit_rate,mode,p50_ms,p95_ms,throughput_tok/s
0.5,streaming,38,210,14200
0.5,nonstream,32,175,15800
0.8,streaming,30,120,16500
0.8,nonstream,29,115,16800

ben: hunch: streaming reduces per-step batch sizes -> kernel selector thrashes -> warmup penalty. Also client readloop backpressure adds jitter. We saw increased proxy CPU sys% at same qps.

maria: did you try pinning the kernel to matmul_fused_v2 for the whole run?

alex: yes. Forcing kernel via env KERNEL_FORCE=matmul_fused_v2 reduced streaming p95 by ~10% (210->190) but mem use +150MB and tail latency still worse than nonstream.

qa-bot: Repro checklist requested by QA:
- bench binary v2.3.1
- model: redwood-open-7b (q8)
- clients: 1000, think-time 20ms, seed=42
- KV service: stubbed with tunable hit-rate

cheng: can we instrument kernel-switch count and attach flamegraphs? need to see time spent in kernel init vs execution.

alex: attached quick profile snippet (inline):
kernel_switches: 87
avg_kernel_init_ms: 1.8
avg_exec_ms: 0.42
proxy_cpu_sys%: 28

ben: proposal: two follow-ups
1) run controlled microbench where we keep batch size constant (override batching heuristic) and compare.
2) test streaming with a small prefix cache (warm KV for first 50 tokens) to raise effective hit-rate and see delta.

maria: +1. Also add a test forcing readloop to yield less frequently (increase client read buffer) — that might reduce kernel churn.

infra-bot: @alex triggered perf-job `readloop-sampling-181345` on perf-cluster (nodes: perf-a1..a3). Logs: https://perf.internal/runs/181345

alex: thanks, kicking off the microbench now. Will paste minimal repro harness and a short script to reproduce.

ben: FYI keep the baseline nonstream config identical (same model, same seq length distribution, same KV stub). We need a strict consistent baseline for this comparison.

alex: noted. will post results in this thread when done :white_check_mark:
